title: 6.1 Perpendicular and Angle Bisectors

icans: I can use the Perpendicular Bisector Theorem and its converse to find lengths.
I can use the Angle Bisector Theorem and its converse to find lengths and angle measures.
I can write an equation of a perpendicular bisector.

vocab: the same ___________ from two or more objects
a line, segment, or ray that is perpendicular to a segment at its ___________
Distance from a point to a line
the length of the ________________ segment from the point to the line
a ray that divides an angle into two ____________ angles

blocks.p: Fold 1. Draw a segment A̅B̅. Fold A onto B. The crease is the perpendicular bisector. Mark three points on the crease and measure.
Fold 2. Draw an angle. Fold one side onto the other. The crease is the angle bisector. Mark a point on it and measure the perpendicular distance to each side.

blocks.sec: Part 2 · Notes and examples (fill in each note, then work the example)

notes: Perpendicular Bisector Theorem: If a point is on the perpendicular bisector of a segment, then it is _______________ from the endpoints of the segment.

blocks.stem: P̅F̅ is the perpendicular bisector of L̅M̅. Find PM.

notes: Converse: If a point is equidistant from the endpoints of a segment, then it is on the _______________ _______________ of the segment.
titles: Converse of the Perpendicular Bisector Theorem

blocks.stem: P̅F̅ is the perpendicular bisector of L̅M̅. Find PL.

notes: Angle Bisector Theorem: If a point is on the bisector of an angle, then it is equidistant from the two _______________ of the angle.
Distance from a point to a line: The distance from a point to a line is the length of the _______________ segment from the point to the line.
titles: Distance from a point to a line

notes: Converse: If a point is in the interior of an angle and is equidistant from the two sides, then it lies on the _______________ of the angle.
titles: Converse of the Angle Bisector Theorem
